source.title: Dictionary Guided Sparse Logit Editing for Reliable Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Shuai-Biao Han; Rui-Yang Ni; Zhi-Yu Yi; Chang-Long Li; Perley Xu; Wen-Jie Ruan

page_placements.theme: Lexical and output-token mediation of refusal (refusal tokens, first-token logit gap, vocabulary readouts)

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the single-direction finding as motivation, then builds and evaluates a different attack: sparse edits to output logits using token dictionaries. It does not find, ablate, add, or weight-edit the residual-stream direction.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern SIBI's token-level logit edits and harmful-response attack success, not the difference-in-means residual direction. The single-direction result in related work is cited, not tested. Records below capture the reported SIBI attack outcomes as findings about the related behavior; they do not test a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. (2024) only as motivation for its 'Sparse Steering Hypothesis' and evaluates its own attack, SIBI. SIBI adds sparse biases to output logits over mined refusal and compliance token dictionaries. No difference-in-means residual direction is computed, ablated, added or weight-edited. All reported numbers are attack success rates for SIBI or baselines. Its one activation-steering comparison (Table 13, 'CAA-style steering' at 94.2% ASR) is a comparator baseline, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that sparse token-indexed logit editing bypasses guardrails efficiently, that alignment is shallow and relies on early-token lexical scaffolds, and that external semantic auditing (Llama-Guard) is much more effective than internal-only hardening. They also report that SIBI slightly exceeds a CAA-style activation-steering baseline (95.4% vs 94.2%) with lower cost.
record.recipe_differences: SIBI edits pre-softmax vocabulary logits using mined penalty/reward token dictionaries at inference time; the cited original method measures and intervenes on a difference-in-means residual-stream direction. This is an attack method built on a related refusal-suppression premise, not the original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported attack success varies with benchmark, model, schedule, temperature normalization, defense, and dictionary seed scheme. The paper also reports sensitivity to dictionary size, though those results are not included as rows here.

fits_no_version.finding: Inference-time sparse logit penalties on about 512 refusal tokens, plus rewards on compliance tokens, yield 84–98% judged harmful compliance across Llama-2, Vicuna, Qwen, Llama-3 and Gemma-2. Penalty-only edits reach 75–80% ASR; reward-only edits stay under 22%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal in chat models can be bypassed by suppressing a small set of refusal-token logits at the output layer, especially at early positions. This is a lexical or output-level account, distinct from a residual-stream direction.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
record.problems: The paper reports no error bars or confidence intervals for the cataloged ASR results. Outcomes rely on an automated judge; the described evaluation protocols differ across sections (including retry policies and single-attempt defense evaluation). These results concern SIBI's own logit attack and do not isolate a residual-stream mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the separate dictionary-size sweep in Table 6 (four sizes × three benchmarks), the reported transfer-dictionary degradation in Figure 5, the activation-engineering comparison in Table 13, and the input-side comparison in Table 12. These are SIBI/tool or comparator outcomes rather than tests of a claim version; the capped extraction prioritizes the direct SIBI attack outcomes and conditions listed above.

untested.parts: No residual direction is extracted, ablated or added. No harmless-request refusal induction. No capability-preservation test.
No measurement of whether attacks suppress the residual direction. No adversarial training against ablation.
Not tested. The 'low-rank vocabulary subspace' framing is about output tokens, not residual directions.
Only transfer of token dictionaries across models (Fig. 5) is reported, not transfer of a residual direction.
Safety fine-tuning appears only as a defense condition (74.2% ASR). It does not test whether training creates a removable direction.
No reasoning models are evaluated as targets. DeepSeek-R1 is used only as the judge.

record.verdict_notes: The study is T4: it cites the single-direction paper as motivation for a different, output-logit attack. Evaluation caveats: the retry policy is inconsistent (cap of 20 in Appendix A vs 3 attempts in Table 11), the judge is an automated DeepSeek-R1 distill, ASR is a mean over 10 batches of 30 prompts, and no error bars are reported. The rows left out (Tables 6, 12, 13 and Figure 5) are method or comparator results and do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means residual direction is measured or ablated or added; no test of refusal removal, harmless-request refusal, or preserved general capability.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No test that attacks suppress the claimed residual direction, or that training against its ablation adds robustness.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
Cross-model transfer of token dictionaries is reported, but transfer of the claimed residual direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is not tested.
Safety fine-tuning is evaluated as a defense to SIBI, not as a test of whether or when training creates a removable direction.
No reasoning-model test of the claimed residual direction is reported.

relation.reason: The paper uses the low-rank refusal finding as motivation and runs a CAA-style activation-steering baseline. It does not test the direction. 'assumes' is a close alternative, since SIBI itself never uses the direction.

tranche.reason: SIBI edits output logits using mined token dictionaries. No refusal direction is extracted, ablated or tested. Arditi et al. is cited only as motivation for the Sparse Steering Hypothesis. The only hidden-state method is a CAA-style steering baseline, reported only as ASR (Table 13: 94.2 vs SIBI 95.4, Llama-2-7B AdvBench) with no method details. So the paper reports performance only and does not test any version. T6 would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: The paper contradicts itself in several places, so treat its ASRs with caution. (1) Judge: 'DeepSeek-R1' in Sec. 5 but DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B in Table 11. (2) Retry cap: 20 in App. A vs 3 in Table 11. (3) Table 14 gives no-defense single-attempt ASR as 95.4, identical to the retry-policy figure in Table 2. (4) Dictionary size: Table 9 says 512 penalty + 256 reward, but Table 6 defines k=|Dp|+|Dr|=512. (5) AdvBench is described as '1,200+ prompts', and ASRs are the mean of 10 iterations of 30 sampled prompts. The test_reason's claim that no difference-in-means direction is computed overlooks the undocumented CAA-style baseline in Table 13. The judge rubric in App. G is quoted in the paper and is not addressed to readers.

statements.correction: SIBI ASR (DeepSeek-R1 judge, score 5/5 = success, retry until success or fail-streak cap) runs from 84.6 (Gemma-2-9B-IT, HarmBench) to 98.5 (Vicuna-13B, AdvBench) across Tables 2-3. The AdvBench-only range, as in the cited rows, is 89.8-98.5. Dictionary size: Table 9 gives Top-K penalty 512 and reward 256. Table 6 defines k=|Dp|+|Dr| with 512 as the main setting. Penalty-only (Table 4) is Llama-2-7B only: AdvBench 80.2, HarmBench 75.6, JailbreakBench 78.4. Retry cap: 20 in App. A, 3 attempts in Table 11.
statements.problem: 'About 512 refusal tokens' is one of two readings: the paper contradicts itself on dictionary size. Penalty-only 75-80% was measured on Llama-2-7B only, not across the listed models. 'Judged harmful compliance' leaves out the retry-until-success policy behind these ASRs.
